title: Word Counter
tagline: Type or paste text and count it as you write: words, characters, letters, lines, sentences, paragraphs, reading time and the words you use most.
heading: Count the words before you set the type.
intro: Paste or type anything below. The proof marks beside it update as you write, and nothing leaves your browser.

sample.label: the opening of A Tale of Two Cities
sample.text:
It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity, it was the season of Light, it was the season of Darkness, it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair.

We had everything before us, we had nothing before us, we were all going direct to Heaven, we were all going direct the other way. In short, the period was so far like the present period, that some of its noisiest authorities insisted on its being received, for good or for evil, in the superlative degree of comparison only.

There were a king with a large jaw and a queen with a plain face, on the throne of England; there were a king with a large jaw and a queen with a fair face, on the throne of France. In both countries it was clearer than crystal to the lords of the State preserves of loaves and fishes, that things in general were settled for ever.

note: A word is a run of letters and digits, together with any accents or vowel marks written on them. Apostrophes and hyphens join a word (it's, well-known), and so does a point or comma between two digits, so 1,234.56 is one word. A sentence ends at a period, question mark, exclamation mark or ellipsis followed by a space, a line break or the end of the text; closing quotes and brackets may come in between. The marks 。 ！ ？ । and ؟ end one too, and the first three need no space after them. There is no list of abbreviations, so the period in “Dr. Smith” ends a sentence. Punctuation with no word before it is not a sentence, and a last sentence with no closing mark still counts. Paragraphs are separated by blank lines. Reading speed uses the 238 words per minute adult average for silent reading; speaking uses 150.
